renderRule: No user-facing text may be hardcoded. Every user-facing label, message, error, empty state, loading state, dialog, notification, email subject/body, CTA, accessibility label and status must render through x()/t() or an equivalent governed localization layer.
englishSourceRule: English source/catalog is authoritative for semantic keys and source copy.
selectedLanguageRule: When an enabled language is selected, that language's governed value is rendered.
missingUnreviewedRule: For a supported non-English locale, a missing, empty, whitespace-only, or explicit [key] value must resolve to the authoritative English catalog value. Unsupported/unavailable locales also use governed English fallback. Native/reviewed translation completion remains separately evidenced.
unavailableLocaleRule: When the selected locale is unsupported/unavailable, or a supported locale value is missing/empty/placeholder, use governed English fallback. A literal [key] must not surface when an English catalog value exists.
languageRegistryRule: Language registry is dynamic and registry-driven; there is no hard-coded 23-language ceiling.
platformContract: Web, Android and iOS use the same localization key and semantic contract.
environmentRule: Development and Production use the same governed localization source; both therefore use the same localization source, key contract, fallback policy, locale registry behavior and UI primitives. Only secrets and external-service activation may differ.
featureMergeGate: no unreviewed non-English production copy in an enabled locale
nativeReviewRule: Native/reviewed status may only be certified from actual evidence; no machine-generated or guessed translation may be promoted to reviewed production copy.
mobileRule: Web, Android and iOS use the same semantic localization key contract.
extensibility: Language registry is dynamic and there is no hard-coded 23-language ceiling.
